usual_baseline: Formal scales are rarely used. GASS completion 5–27%, 7% on inpatient wards [3408]. AIMS in 9.1% of long-term antipsychotic patients [3124]. Side effects are noted informally in 96% of notes, but with no scale [3315].
fix_that_works: A new pharmacy team and guideline awareness raised six-monthly GASS from 5% to 75% [3620]. Sharing findings and recording scores on depot charts and SystmOne took GASS from 26.6% to 55.17% [3332].
fix_that_fails: Ward QI presentations and an infographic moved inpatient GASS only from 7% to 26% [3408]. Rating scale use rose only from 0% to 24% [3315]. Yearly GASS fell from 88% to 53% on the fourth re-audit when face-to-face reviews stopped [3702].
consultant_advice: Commonly audited and the baseline is always poor. Gains depend on someone owning the task, such as pharmacy or depot clinics. More useful to audit whether an abnormal score led to a change in treatment, or tardive dyskinesia screening, which is rarely measured.
